classification.difficultyReason: Compare aligned place values, including implicit trailing zeros, and explain the explicitly taught first-differing-digit strategy.

questions.mappingNote: Each comparison and the reflection assess decimal ordering. order-decimals-3dp is the closest supplied skill; the source includes two longer decimals, retained exactly.
questions.methodNote: Page 2 establishes decimal place value. Page 4 compares positions on number lines, with the larger number farther right. Page 5 explicitly teaches aligning decimal points and comparing digits from left to right.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Compare positive decimals by place value and explain a comparison strategy; two source numbers extend beyond three decimal places.

classification.difficultyReason: Construct ten different decimals while satisfying restrictions on digit use.

questions.mappingNote: The decimal place-value explanation on page 2 supports reading and constructing these decimals. The closest catalogue skill concerns expressing decimals to thousandths; the sample answers all use three decimal places.
questions.methodNote: Use decimal place value and the decimal point to construct numbers from the specified digits.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Construct ten different decimals while satisfying restrictions on digit use.

classification.difficultyReason: Apply left-to-right place-value comparison, treating absent decimal digits as zeros when a shorter decimal shares the initial digits.

questions.mappingNote: Every pair directly assesses decimal comparison. The supplied comparison skill is the closest catalogue match, although some source values have four or five decimal places.
questions.methodNote: Example 6 aligns decimal points and compares digits from left to right, stopping at the first differing digit. Decimal place-value definitions support interpreting additional places and trailing zeros.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Compare positive decimals by the first differing place-value digit; several pairs extend beyond three decimal places.

classification.difficultyReason: Arrange five values by successive place-value comparisons, resolving matching tenths and equivalent trailing-zero forms.

questions.mappingNote: Question 8 directly assesses decimal ordering. The closest supplied skill is order-decimals-3dp, although parts c and d extend beyond three decimal places.
questions.methodNote: Align decimal points and compare digits from left to right, beginning with whole-number places. Trailing zeros do not change a decimal's value.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Order positive decimals with unequal lengths, internal zeros and up to seven decimal places.

classification.difficultyReason: Compare each decimal with the midpoint between two consecutive whole numbers.

questions.mappingNote: Question 9 applies decimal comparison to proximity to consecutive whole numbers. The rounding skill is the closest catalogue match; longer decimals use the same taught comparison method.
questions.methodNote: Use decimal place value and compare digits from left to right. The midpoint 4.5 separates numbers closer to 4 from those closer to 5.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Compare each decimal with the midpoint between two consecutive whole numbers.

classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied 0.6-unit equivalence to determine how many smaller or larger place-value units represent the same quantity.

questions.mappingNote: Question 10 directly assesses equivalent quantities across powers-of-ten units. Page 2 provides the place-value chart and decimal-fraction relationships; supplied part c anchors the conversion in units. Comparison material on pages 4–5 is contextual.
questions.methodNote: Use the base-ten place-value relationships: write six tenths as 0.6 units, then express that quantity in the requested place-value unit.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Express the same decimal quantity using different powers-of-ten place-value units.

classification.difficultyReason: Convert the supplied 0.89 units into counts of the requested place-value units, choosing the appropriate power-of-ten scaling direction.

questions.mappingNote: The task directly assesses equivalent quantities across place-value units, best matched by multiplying and dividing decimals by powers of 10.
questions.methodNote: Use the base-ten place-value relationships: express 89 hundredths as 0.89 units, then convert to the requested place-value unit.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Convert one fixed quantity between named decimal and whole-number place-value units.

classification.difficultyReason: Use the completed 0.723-unit statement to rescale into hundredths, tenths and larger units while preserving the quantity.

questions.mappingNote: Converting between thousandths, hundredths, tenths and whole-number place-value units directly assesses multiplication and division by powers of ten. The supplied completed part c anchors the method.
questions.methodNote: Use decimal place value: 723 thousandths is 0.723 units. Divide this quantity by the value of the requested unit, using the powers-of-ten place-value chart.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Express the same decimal quantity in different place-value units using powers of ten.

classification.difficultyReason: Direct conversion of fractions with power-of-ten denominators, including mixed numerals.

questions.mappingNote: Every part assesses fraction-to-decimal conversion. Mixed numerals require retaining the whole-number part; h, m and o extend the same place-value method to ten-thousandths.
questions.methodNote: Read the fractional part using the power-of-ten denominator and retain the whole-number part. Page 3 Example 3 demonstrates place-value conversion; page 8 explicitly demonstrates converting a mixed numeral with a power-of-ten denominator.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Direct conversion of fractions with power-of-ten denominators, including mixed numerals.

classification.difficultyReason: Determine fraction–decimal equivalences in both directions and identify the missing digit in each representation, using the supplied digit set as a constraint.

questions.mappingNote: All six parts assess fraction–decimal conversion by recovering a missing digit. This is the closest supplied taxonomy skill.
questions.methodNote: Write decimals as fractions with power-of-ten denominators and simplify; convert fractions to equivalent fractions with power-of-ten denominators. Page 9 also supplies familiar fraction–decimal equivalences.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Complete familiar fraction–decimal equivalences by identifying one missing digit.

classification.difficultyReason: Match five familiar terminating decimals to their equivalent unit fractions.

questions.mappingNote: The task directly assesses matching decimal and fraction representations; the available conversion skill is the closest catalogue match.
questions.methodNote: Write the decimal as a fraction with a power-of-ten denominator, then simplify. Page 9 also supplies familiar decimal–fraction equivalents.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Match five familiar terminating decimals to their equivalent unit fractions.

classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the second parcel as the total minus the known weight, then align decimal places and subtract with regrouping.

questions.mappingNote: The total and first parcel's weight are given; subtracting the first weight from the total directly assesses decimal subtraction in a word problem.
questions.methodNote: Use the vertical subtraction algorithm with decimal points aligned. Append a zero to match decimal places and regroup as required.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Find one missing weight using a single decimal subtraction.

classification.difficultyReason: Combine two decimal lengths and subtract their total from the original length.

questions.mappingNote: Question 4 applies the methods of Examples 10 and 11: first add the two lengths cut, then subtract their total from the original timber length.
questions.methodNote: Use vertical decimal addition and subtraction with decimal points aligned, adding trailing zeros to equalise decimal places.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Combine two decimal lengths and subtract their total from the original length.

classification.difficultyReason: Interpret being behind a race record as a time difference and subtract the record from each finishing time, retaining seconds.

questions.mappingNote: Each requested delay is the girl's finishing time minus 11.47 s. This directly assesses decimal subtraction in a word problem; all values are already in seconds.
questions.methodNote: Pages 11–12 teach decimal subtraction by aligning decimal points and place-value columns, adding trailing zeros when needed, and using the standard subtraction algorithm.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Identify and calculate three decimal time differences from one common record time.

classification.difficultyReason: Add three decimal distances and subtract their total from the team distance.

questions.mappingNote: Question 6 applies the taught decimal algorithms to find a missing distance from a known total; decimal word problems is the closest directly assessed skill.
questions.methodNote: Use decimal addition and subtraction with decimal points and place-value columns aligned, adding trailing zeros where needed, as taught on pages 11–12.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Add three decimal distances and subtract their total from the team distance.

classification.difficultyReason: Convert two distances from metres to kilometres, then add all five journey stages.

questions.mappingNote: The task applies decimal addition to a journey after converting the two metre distances into kilometres. Decimal word problems are the primary assessed skill; metric length conversion is secondary.
questions.methodNote: Pages 11–12 teach decimal addition using the standard vertical algorithm with decimal points and place-value columns aligned.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Convert two distances from metres to kilometres, then add all five journey stages.

classification.difficultyReason: Identify the original length by adding four equal decimal lengths and the leftover length.

questions.mappingNote: The original roll comprises all four removed pieces plus the leftover string. Repeated addition applies the exercise's taught decimal-addition method directly.
questions.methodNote: Pages 11–12 teach vertical decimal addition with decimal points and place-value columns aligned, adding trailing zeros when needed.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Identify the original length by adding four equal decimal lengths and the leftover length.

classification.difficultyReason: Direct application of the taught decimal-place shifts by one, two or three places.

questions.mappingNote: All twelve parts directly assess multiplication or division by 10, 100 or 1000, so decimal-times-divide-powers-10 is the closest exact catalogue match.
questions.methodNote: Pages 13–15 teach multiplying and dividing by powers of 10 by moving the decimal point the corresponding number of places and inserting zeros when necessary. Examples 12–15 provide the applicable method. Page 20 was inspected but its general division methods are not needed.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Direct application of the taught decimal-place shifts by one, two or three places.

classification.difficultyReason: Interpret equal sharing as division by 10 and apply the taught decimal place-value shift.

questions.mappingNote: Equal sharing among 10 people requires dividing the monetary amount by 10. The directly assessed calculation matches the powers-of-10 skill; the later general division methods on page 20 are unnecessary.
questions.methodNote: Page 14 explains division by 10 as moving the decimal point one place left and demonstrates it in Example 14; page 15 repeats this rule in the summary.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Interpret equal sharing as division by 10 and apply the taught decimal place-value shift.

classification.difficultyReason: Scale a production rate by powers of 10 and convert seconds to minutes in part a.

questions.mappingNote: The shared production stem makes rate scaling the primary assessed skill. Parts a and b scale by 100 and one tenth respectively; part c recognises a tenfold time interval. Part a also assesses seconds-to-minutes conversion.
questions.methodNote: Pages 13–15 demonstrate multiplication and division by powers of 10 using decimal place value. Page 20 demonstrates decimal division. Apply proportional scaling to the production quantities; part a additionally requires 60 seconds = 1 minute, which is not explicitly demonstrated in these supplied teaching pages.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Scale a production rate by powers of 10 and convert seconds to minutes in part a.

classification.difficultyReason: Combines metric length conversions with the squared conversion factor required for area.

questions.mappingNote: Parts a–d use metric length conversion and powers-of-10 scaling; parts e–g additionally assess squared conversion factors, making convert-area-units the most advanced directly assessed skill.
questions.methodNote: Pages 13–15 demonstrate multiplication and division by powers of 10 using place value. Page 20 demonstrates decimal division. None explicitly teaches metric length conversion factors or squaring a length conversion factor for area.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Combines metric length conversions with the squared conversion factor required for area.

classification.difficultyReason: Convert terminating decimals to fractions and multiply without cancelling.

questions.mappingNote: All twelve parts explicitly require the fraction method; decimal multiplication is the primary assessed operation.
questions.methodNote: Example 16 converts decimals to place-value fractions, multiplies without cancelling, then converts the product to a decimal.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Convert terminating decimals to fractions and multiply without cancelling.

classification.difficultyReason: Multiply whole numbers by terminating decimals and restore the decimal point.

questions.mappingNote: Each part multiplies a whole number by a decimal; placing the decimal point is the directly assessed method.
questions.methodNote: Following Example 17(a), multiply as whole numbers, then restore the total number of decimal places in the factors.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Multiply whole numbers by terminating decimals and restore the decimal point.

classification.difficultyReason: Multiply decimal factors, including two multi-digit products, and place the decimal point correctly.

questions.mappingNote: Parts a–e and g–l multiply two decimals; part f multiplies a decimal by a whole number. All directly apply the decimal-point placement method.
questions.methodNote: Multiply integer digits, then place the decimal point using the sum of the decimal places in the factors, as demonstrated in Example 17. Its unrelated integer factors in part (c) are not propagated.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Multiply decimal factors, including two multi-digit products, and place the decimal point correctly.

classification.difficultyReason: Complete decimal products across a table spanning several powers of ten.

questions.mappingNote: The table repeatedly applies the decimal-product method and multiplication by powers of ten.
questions.methodNote: Multiply as whole numbers and place the decimal point using the combined decimal places; retain zeros needed for place value.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Complete decimal products across a table spanning several powers of ten.

classification.difficultyReason: Direct decimal multiplication using the method demonstrated in Example 17.

questions.mappingNote: All nine products directly assess the method in Example 17, including leading and removable trailing zeros.
questions.methodNote: Multiply the corresponding whole numbers, then use the total decimal places in the factors to place the decimal point.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Direct decimal multiplication using the method demonstrated in Example 17.

classification.difficultyReason: Find one tenth of whole numbers and decimals.

questions.mappingNote: The six responses directly assess scaling by one tenth.
questions.methodNote: Multiplication by 0.1 is multiplication by one tenth; this agrees with placing one additional decimal place in the product.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Find one tenth of whole numbers and decimals.

classification.difficultyReason: Find one hundredth of whole numbers and decimals, retaining necessary zeros.

questions.mappingNote: All six parts assess scaling by one hundredth rather than general multistep multiplication.
questions.methodNote: Multiplication by 0.01 is multiplication by one hundredth, consistent with the decimal-place rule.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Find one hundredth of whole numbers and decimals, retaining necessary zeros.

classification.difficultyReason: Multiplication by one thousandth is division by 1000, including products requiring leading zeros.

questions.mappingNote: Division by the power of ten 1000 is the closest catalogue match for all six scaling tasks.
questions.methodNote: Multiplication by 0.001 is multiplication by one thousandth; the product has three additional decimal places before removing trailing zeros.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Multiplication by one thousandth is division by 1000, including products requiring leading zeros.

classification.difficultyReason: Multiply a quantity by its unit price and present the resulting cost to the nearest cent.

questions.mappingNote: Each part applies a unit rate to a decimal quantity. Page 26 supplies rounding context, and the teacher answers establish nearest-cent presentation.
questions.methodNote: Multiply quantity by price per unit using whole-number multiplication and the decimal-place rule; round money to two decimal places using the next digit.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Multiply a quantity by its unit price and present the resulting cost to the nearest cent.

classification.difficultyReason: Apply the same decimal-divisor scaling rule to six given numbers.

questions.mappingNote: All six parts directly assess conversion of decimal divisors to whole numbers; the resulting powers-of-ten scaling is secondary.
questions.methodNote: Multiply the dividend and divisor by the same power of 10 to make the divisor a whole number, as demonstrated in Method 1 and Example 20. Here each divisor becomes 1.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Apply the same decimal-divisor scaling rule to six given numbers.

classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied division fact and diagonal answers to scale quotients by powers of ten, distinguishing the effects of changing the dividend and divisor. The grid repeats this direct place-value application.

questions.mappingNote: The complete grid assesses decimal division, especially preserving a quotient when both operands are scaled together; the given diagonal anchors the related facts.
questions.methodNote: Use the division algorithm for whole-number divisors; for decimal divisors multiply dividend and divisor by the same power of 10. Apply related facts and place-value scaling across and down the grid.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Complete a division grid using the supplied related fact and systematic changes in place value.

classification.difficultyReason: Interpret price per litre as total cost divided by volume, then perform the taught decimal-by-whole-number division and state the monetary unit rate.

questions.mappingNote: The total cost and fuel volume determine a unit rate; the required calculation is 13.56 divided by 12.
questions.methodNote: Divide a decimal by a whole number using the ordinary division algorithm, keeping the decimal point aligned, as in Example 18 and the division summary.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Find a unit price by dividing a decimal total cost by a whole-number volume.

classification.difficultyReason: Interpret timber required per frame as a rate and divide by a decimal.

questions.mappingNote: The number of frames is the total timber length divided by the length required for each frame; scaling both quantities by 10 gives 968 divided by 8.
questions.methodNote: Multiply the dividend and divisor by the same power of 10 to make the divisor a whole number, then divide, as demonstrated in Example 20.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Interpret timber required per frame as a rate and divide by a decimal.

classification.difficultyReason: Convert five familiar fractions to terminating decimals using equivalent fractions.

questions.mappingNote: Each assigned fraction has a terminating decimal and directly assesses fraction-to-decimal conversion. Equivalent fractions follow the supplied teaching without introducing recurring notation or rounding.
questions.methodNote: Example 8 converts fractions by multiplying numerator and denominator to obtain a power-of-ten denominator. Page 23 explicitly demonstrates 1/40 = 25/1000 = 0.025. Division is also taught on page 9; pages 23–24 distinguish terminating and recurring decimals.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Convert five familiar fractions to terminating decimals using equivalent fractions.

classification.difficultyReason: Use division to distinguish terminating results from recurring results and identify where repetition begins after initial non-recurring digits. These are direct decisions within the taught algorithm.

questions.mappingNote: All eleven parts convert fractions to decimals, including terminating results and one-digit cycles following non-recurring digits. Examples 9 and 21–23 supply the division method and recurring notation.
questions.methodNote: Divide the numerator by the denominator using short division. A repeated remainder identifies the recurring cycle; use dots above recurring digits. Stop when the remainder is zero.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Direct conversions of sixths and twelfths using division and recurring notation.

classification.difficultyReason: Convert six sevenths to recurring decimals and recognise their common cyclic digit pattern.

questions.mappingNote: This task applies the demonstrated sevenths conversion to all six proper fractions with denominator 7 and asks students to identify the cyclic relationship.
questions.methodNote: Divide numerator by denominator using the division process; continue until a remainder repeats, then mark the first and last digits of the recurring cycle with dots. Page 24 Example 23 explicitly demonstrates division of 3 by 7.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Convert six sevenths to recurring decimals and recognise their common cyclic digit pattern.

classification.difficultyReason: Direct conversion of fractions with power-of-ten denominators, including ten-thousandths.

questions.mappingNote: Fraction-to-decimal conversion is the closest catalogue skill covering all fourteen parts, including four decimal places.
questions.methodNote: Read power-of-ten denominators as decimal places; partition numerators into place-value fractions when needed, following Example 3. The place-value chart extends this method to ten-thousandths.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Direct conversion of fractions with power-of-ten denominators, including ten-thousandths.

classification.difficultyReason: Identify the value represented by a specified digit using decimal place-value columns; includes ten-thousandths.

questions.mappingNote: The selected skill is the closest catalogue match for identifying decimal digit values. This question extends its three-place description to ten-thousandths.
questions.methodNote: Use the place-value chart to locate a digit, then multiply the digit by its column value. Page 2 includes ten-thousandths and smaller places; Example 1 on page 3 expands a decimal by place value.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Identify the value represented by a specified digit using decimal place-value columns; includes ten-thousandths.

classification.difficultyReason: Identify the value contributed by a specified digit; the final two numbers extend the same place-value method beyond thousandths.

questions.mappingNote: Each part directly assesses interpreting a digit's decimal place value. The closest supplied skill is express-thousandths-decimals, with the same method extended to four and five decimal places.
questions.methodNote: Use the decimal place-value chart to identify the digit's column, then express its contribution as the digit multiplied by that column's fractional unit. Page 2 extends the chart through millionths; Example 1 on page 3 models expansion by place value.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Identify the value contributed by a specified digit; the final two numbers extend the same place-value method beyond thousandths.

classification.difficultyReason: Direct comparison of positive decimals using the first differing place; some numbers extend beyond three decimal places.

questions.mappingNote: The task directly assesses decimal comparison. order-decimals-3dp is the closest catalogue skill, although several givens have more decimal places.
questions.methodNote: Align decimal points and compare digits from left to right. The first unequal place determines the larger number; trailing zeros preserve value.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Direct comparison of positive decimals using the first differing place; some numbers extend beyond three decimal places.

classification.difficultyReason: Compare corresponding decimal places, treating omitted trailing places as zeros, and arrange each set in descending order. Shared prefixes require closer comparison but no new method.

questions.mappingNote: Ordering decimal sets directly assesses decimal comparison. The closest catalogue skill is order-decimals-3dp, although this source also includes four-place decimals.
questions.methodNote: Align decimal points and compare corresponding digits from left to right, starting with the whole-number parts.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Compare positive decimals by place value; some values extend to four decimal places.

classification.difficultyReason: Inspect the tenths digit to choose the nearest whole number, including carrying 299 up to 300. Later decimal digits do not change the decision.

questions.mappingNote: The rounding rule applies directly to the units place in each part.
questions.methodNote: Inspect the digit immediately right of the rounding place; increase the rounding digit for 5–9 and otherwise retain it.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Round positive decimals to the nearest whole number, including one carry across 299.

classification.difficultyReason: Choose the power-of-ten denominator from decimal place value, simplify by common factors and retain whole-number parts where present. Each part follows the supplied conversion method.

questions.mappingNote: Example 7 supplies the conversion and simplification method for all twelve parts.
questions.methodNote: Write the decimal over a power of 10 and simplify; preserve whole-number parts as mixed numerals.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Convert terminating decimals using place-value denominators and simplify.

classification.difficultyReason: Select useful simplification or denominator scaling, then read the equivalent decimal while preserving mixed-number whole parts. The hardest parts link these routine steps, including scaling sixteenths to ten-thousandths.

questions.mappingNote: Example 8 supplies the denominator-scaling method; the same method extends to denominator 16 using 10000.
questions.methodNote: Simplify when useful, obtain an equivalent denominator that is a power of 10, then read the decimal; retain the integer part of mixed numerals.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Convert fractions and mixed numerals by simplifying or scaling denominators, including sixteenths.

classification.difficultyReason: Convert or recognise each fraction's decimal equivalent, interpreting recurring dots and mixed-number whole parts, then select its match from the supplied choices.

questions.mappingNote: The two table rows are independently ordered lists; matching requires conversion rather than reading vertical pairs.
